title: Living faith as aggregate: includes love, desire, trust — will also subject (Galatians 5:6)
source_text: XXIII. Sed ut plurimum fidei nomine, tum in Scriptura, tum apud scriptores Ecclesiasticos, designatur aggregatum quoddam pluribus actibus vel habitibus constans, & quod praeter jam dictum assensum, includit synceram Dei dilectionem, & ardens gratiae ejus desiderium, ac fiduciam qua ad Deum confugimus, & in favore ejus acquiescimus. Et haec est quam fidem vivam, salvificam & justificantem, solemus appellare, & quae a Paulo dicitur fides per dilectionem operans, quamque Schola Romana fidem formatam vocat. Fidei autem sic acceptae subjectum non est sola mens, sed etiam voluntas, cujus actus est Dei amor, & desiderium gratiae divinae, ac fiducia qua Deo innitimur & illi adhaeremus.
pass_a_gloss: But most often by the name of faith, both in Scripture and among ecclesiastical writers, there is designated a certain aggregate consisting of several acts or habits, which besides the assent already named includes sincere love of God, and ardent desire of His grace, and the trust by which we flee to God and rest in His favor. And this is what we usually call living, saving, and justifying faith, and which Paul calls faith working through love, and which the Roman school calls formed faith. But of faith so taken the subject is not mind alone but also the will, whose act is love of God and desire of divine grace and the trust by which we lean on God and cling to Him.
pass_b_english: Usually 'faith' names an aggregate: assent plus love, desire of grace, and resting trust.
That living/saving/formed faith (faith working through love, Galatians 5:6) has will as subject too.

choices.why: Complex of acts/habits under one name.
